arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mary Williams argued the factfinding here differs from prior cases.
She stated the Court struck down similar sentencing changes before.
Justice Scalia questioned if this fact is more significant than others.
He noted it could lengthen the sentence enormously for the defendant.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests whether a judge can decide facts that increase a prison term without a jury.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 23, lines 19-41

sections.heading: How the case got here
paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on October 14, 2008.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 3, lines 7-15

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Oregon wants judges to set consecutive sentences without a jury.
The defendant wants a jury to find facts before sentences run back-to-back.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 23, lines 19-41

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Oregon argues this factfinding differs from previous Sixth Amendment cases.
The defendant argues this is a bright-line rule from Apprendi.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Scalia asked if the sentence length fact is more important than jury facts.
Justice Kennedy asked why the statute requires this specific finding.
